title: BlueWallet
description: Build and inspect a wallet-learning demo covering address validation, transaction planning, wallet adapters, and defensive refusal of incomplete transaction broadcast.
problem: Learners need a source-grounded way to understand and extend BlueWallet while separating implemented behavior from demo data, simulations, and missing integrations.
audience: Third-year undergraduate students who have completed introductory programming and want a practical mobile mini-project.
stack: Electrum JSON-RPC adapter with React Native WebSocket transport (not operational as configured)
prerequisites: Git basics and ability to run the platform tooling described in the source README
learning_outcomes: Explain and trace transaction shape, satoshi formatting, seeded records, and tab shell in its named source files.
Explain and trace bech32 checksum and witness program validation; base58 prefix/length screening; accepted address boundary in its named source files.
Explain and trace sha-256 implementation and electrum script hash preparation in its named source files.
Explain and trace utxo selection, fee estimate, amount validation, and unsigned output construction in its named source files.
Explain and trace walletcore boundary, demowalletcore, electrumwalletcore, and websocket transport in its named source files.
Explain and trace unsignedtransaction type, signing gap, refusal path, and no-send regression test in its named source files.
Explain and trace key/value adapter, json parsing, corrupt state, and local transaction storage in its named source files.
Explain and trace validation-to-plan flow, explicit limitations, test evidence, and release boundary in its named source files.
Distinguish unit-test evidence from device, service, and deployment evidence.
Propose a safe, bounded extension without describing it as already implemented.
